content:
Cook visited Apple's Battersea campus in London this week, where he met with King Charles, as part of a new partnership between Apple and The King's Trust.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also sat down for an in-depth interview with The Independent, discussing this partnership and his feelings during his first month serving as Apple's executive chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO last month, handing the reins to John Ternus. In this week's interview, Cook said the transition 'actually began several years ago.'

Ternus assumed the CEO role right as the iPhone Duo was launching, and Cook noted that the product had already been fully planned out. He explained: 'I wanted to give John a tailwind, and at Apple, tailwinds basically come from the product cycle.'

Cook also emphasised that, as executive chairman, he focuses on 'global policy' matters, and noted that there is a 'very high degree of trust' between him and Ternus. Cook is helping Ternus in whatever way he deems appropriate, but stressed that he 'will not interfere.'

What advice did Cook give Ternus? 'Don't try to be me.' The full interview is available to read in The Independent, which also details the new partnership between Apple and The King's Trust.
